sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantham.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: 2,000 years ago, in ancient Greece, a local ruler had a problem.
sentences.zh: 两千年前，在古希腊，一位地方统治者遇到了一个难题。

sentences.en: He suspected his new crown was not made of solid gold, but he couldn't prove it.
sentences.zh: 他怀疑自己的新王冠不是纯金做的，但他无法证明。

sentences.en: So he asked the kingdom's most famous mathematician, Archimedes, to investigate.
sentences.zh: 于是他请王国里最著名的数学家阿基米德去调查。

sentences.en: While pondering this puzzle, Archimedes took a bath.
sentences.zh: 在思考这个难题时，阿基米德去洗了个澡。

sentences.en: He filled the tub to the brim, and as he stepped in, the water overflowed.
sentences.zh: 他把浴缸装满水，当他坐进去时，水溢了出来。

sentences.en: Archimedes had a flash of insight.
sentences.zh: 阿基米德灵光一现。

sentences.en: The water that spilled out of the bath reflected the volume of his own body.
sentences.zh: 从浴缸里溢出的水反映了他自己身体的体积。

sentences.en: He realized that if he put the crown into water, he could measure its volume by seeing how much water was displaced.
sentences.zh: 他意识到，如果把王冠放进水里，通过观察溢出的水量，就能测量出它的体积。

sentences.en: He could use this to tell the difference between a crown made of pure gold and one that had impurities.
sentences.zh: 他可以利用这一点来分辨纯金王冠和掺了杂质的王冠。

sentences.en: He was so excited with his discovery that he leaped out of the tub and ran naked through the streets,
sentences.zh: 他因这一发现而兴奋不已，以至于跳出浴缸，赤身裸体地跑上街头，

sentences.en: shouting, Eureka, Eureka, which is Greek for, I found it, I found it.
sentences.zh: 大喊着“尤里卡，尤里卡”，在希腊语中意为“我找到了，我找到了”。

sentences.en: The famous story of the Eureka moment may or may not have happened.
sentences.zh: 这个著名的“尤里卡时刻”的故事可能发生过，也可能没有。

sentences.en: It was written 200 years after Archimedes died.
sentences.zh: 它是在阿基米德去世200年后才被写下来的。

sentences.en: But it says something profound about our minds.
sentences.zh: 但它深刻地揭示了我们大脑的某种特质。

sentences.en: A good explanation gives us pleasure.
sentences.zh: 一个好的解释能带给我们愉悦感。

sentences.en: And when we can't come up with a good explanation, we feel dissatisfied.
sentences.zh: 而当我们无法得出一个好的解释时，我们会感到不满。

sentences.en: Something in the human mind yearns to make sense of the world.
sentences.zh: 人类大脑中有一种渴望去理解世界的本能。

sentences.en: Some researchers think this sense-making drive is a basic human impulse,
sentences.zh: 一些研究人员认为，这种寻求意义的驱动力是一种基本的人类冲动，

sentences.en: no different than thirst or hunger.
sentences.zh: 与口渴或饥饿并无不同。

sentences.en: This week on Hidden Brain, we begin a three-part series about our need to explain the world
sentences.zh: 本周在《隐藏的大脑》节目中，我们将开始一个三部分的系列节目，探讨我们解释世界的需要，

sentences.en: and how the stories we tell ourselves can lead to discovery, delight, and disaster.
sentences.zh: 以及我们讲述的故事如何引领我们走向发现、快乐和灾难。

sentences.en: Why is my friend late?
sentences.zh: 为什么我的朋友迟到了？

sentences.en: How does nuclear fission work?
sentences.zh: 核裂变是如何工作的？

sentences.en: What exactly is happening when I sneeze?
sentences.zh: 我打喷嚏时到底发生了什么？

sentences.en: Human beings have an endless number of questions.
sentences.zh: 人类有无穷无尽的问题。

sentences.en: At Princeton University, psychologist Tanya Lombroso is interested in why we come up
sentences.zh: 在普林斯顿大学，心理学家坦尼娅·隆布罗佐对我们为何会提出

sentences.en: with all these questions and how our drive to make sense of the world
sentences.zh: 所有这些问题，以及我们寻求理解世界的驱动力如何

sentences.en: reveals something fundamental about our minds.
sentences.zh: 揭示我们大脑的基本特质很感兴趣。

sentences.en: Tanya Lombroso, welcome to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 坦尼娅·隆布罗佐，欢迎来到《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for having me.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢邀请我来。

sentences.en: Tanya, I want to start with a personal mystery you once encountered in your own life.
sentences.zh: 坦尼娅，我想从你生活中曾经遇到的一个个人谜题开始谈起。

sentences.en: Your toddler returned home from preschool one day
sentences.zh: 你的幼儿有一天从幼儿园回家时，

sentences.en: wearing different pants than the ones she wore in the morning.
sentences.zh: 穿的裤子和早上出门时不一样。

sentences.en: Tell me how the rest of this mystery unfolded.
sentences.zh: 告诉我这个谜题后来是怎么解开的。

sentences.en: So that observation in itself wasn't so surprising.
sentences.zh: 其实，那个观察本身并不令人惊讶。

sentences.en: Toddlers have accidents of all kinds all the time.
sentences.zh: 幼儿总是会发生各种各样的意外。

sentences.en: And so it was pretty familiar that you might have different pants
sentences.zh: 所以，孩子换了裤子是很常见的事，

sentences.en: because your potty-training child might have had an accident.
sentences.zh: 因为正在进行如厕训练的孩子可能会尿裤子。

sentences.en: But at this point, my toddler had been very well potty-trained for months
sentences.zh: 但在当时，我的孩子已经非常成功地完成了几个月的如厕训练，

sentences.en: and hadn't had an accident.
sentences.zh: 而且一直没有发生过意外。

sentences.en: And so on Monday, this was a little surprising.
sentences.zh: 所以周一发生这种事，确实有点令人惊讶。

sentences.en: But it was even more surprising when we went back to pick her up on Tuesday
sentences.zh: 但更令人惊讶的是，当我们周二去接她时，

sentences.en: and found, again, that she had different pants on and had another accident.
sentences.zh: 发现她又换了裤子，又发生了一次意外。

sentences.en: And then on Wednesday, and then on Thursday.
sentences.zh: 接着是周三，然后是周四。

sentences.en: So I found the teacher and said, what's going on?
sentences.zh: 所以我找到了老师，问到底是怎么回事？

sentences.en: She was perfectly potty-trained.
sentences.zh: 她已经完全掌握了如厕训练。

sentences.en: What happened?
sentences.zh: 发生了什么？

sentences.en: And the teacher explained that on Monday, she'd made an interesting observation
sentences.zh: 老师解释说，周一的时候，她观察到一个有趣的现象，

sentences.en: that the girls peed sitting down, but the boys peed standing up.
sentences.zh: 那就是女孩坐着尿尿，而男孩站着尿尿。

sentences.en: And she'd thought to herself, I want to learn how to do that too.
sentences.zh: 于是她心想，我也想学那样做。

sentences.en: And so all week, she had been practicing peeing standing up.
sentences.zh: 所以整个星期，她都在练习站着尿尿。

sentences.en: Now, this is a really charming story,
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常迷人的故事，

sentences.en: but I want to draw your attention to Tanya's thought process as the week unfolded.
sentences.zh: 但我希望大家关注坦尼娅在这一周里的思维过程。

sentences.en: On Monday, when her child came home wearing different pants,
sentences.zh: 周一，当孩子穿着不同的裤子回家时，

sentences.en: she came up with one explanation.
sentences.zh: 她想出了一个解释。

sentences.en: Her daughter had had an accident.
sentences.zh: 她的女儿尿裤子了。

sentences.en: But when the same thing happened on Tuesday and Wednesday,
sentences.zh: 但当周二和周三同样的事情再次发生时，

sentences.en: Tanya came up with a different explanation.
sentences.zh: 坦尼娅想出了一个不同的解释。

sentences.en: Maybe her daughter was regressing on her potty training.
sentences.zh: 也许她女儿的如厕训练退步了。

sentences.en: Finally, when the teacher explained what was going on,
sentences.zh: 最后，当老师解释了事情的原委后，

sentences.en: Tanya now had one simple story that unified and explained everything.
sentences.zh: 坦尼娅终于有了一个简单明了的故事，将一切都串联并解释清楚了。

sentences.en: As a researcher, Tanya is fascinated by how our minds yearn for such stories and explanations
sentences.zh: 作为一名研究人员，坦尼娅对我们的大脑如何渴望这样的故事和解释，

sentences.en: and what happens when we can't find them.
sentences.zh: 以及当我们找不到这些解释时会发生什么，感到非常着迷。

sentences.en: And one very mundane example that I can think of is the experience I had when I was
sentences.zh: 我能想到的一个非常平凡的例子，是我在伯克利担任教授时，

sentences.en: trying to find parking as a professor at Berkeley, where I taught for many years.
sentences.zh: 尝试寻找停车位的经历，我在那里教书多年。

sentences.en: And people who live in the area know that parking can be a challenge.
sentences.zh: 住在那附近的人都知道，停车可能是一个挑战。

sentences.en: And so I would develop all of these pet theories that maybe if it was noon on a Tuesday,
sentences.zh: 所以我总结出了一套套“个人理论”，比如如果是在周二中午，

sentences.en: then this particular parking lot was probably a good place to park.
sentences.zh: 那么这个特定的停车场可能是一个好地方。

sentences.en: Because at noon, I bet the law school professors go out to lunch.
sentences.zh: 因为在中午，我敢打赌法学院的教授们都出去吃午饭了。

sentences.en: But the engineers, they probably don't go out to lunch.
sentences.zh: 但工程系的教授们，他们可能不会出去吃午饭。

sentences.en: So I shouldn't try the lot by engineering.
sentences.zh: 所以我应该避开工程系旁边的停车场。

sentences.en: And so I would develop these pet theories to try to figure out what was going on.
sentences.zh: 于是我就会制定这些个人理论来试图弄清楚到底发生了什么。

sentences.en: And perhaps a given pet theory would work for a week or two.
sentences.zh: 也许某个个人理论能管用一两周。

sentences.en: But then by week three, it no longer worked.
sentences.zh: 但到了第三周，它就不再奏效了。

sentences.en: And I had to say, maybe there's not much patterns here.
sentences.zh: 我不得不说，也许这里并没有什么规律。

sentences.en: Maybe I'm picking up on noise.
sentences.zh: 也许我只是在捕捉噪音。

sentences.en: You cite the evolutionary biologist Stephen Jay Gould, who once said that humans were primates
sentences.zh: 你引用了进化生物学家斯蒂芬·杰伊·古尔德的话，他说人类是

sentences.en: who tell stories.
sentences.zh: 会讲故事的灵长类动物。

sentences.en: What's the connection between the world of stories and the world of explanations?
sentences.zh: 故事的世界和解释的世界之间有什么联系？

sentences.en: I think both stories and explanations are ways that we really try to make sense of or
sentences.zh: 我认为故事和解释都是我们真正试图去理解或

sentences.en: understand the world around us.
sentences.zh: 弄懂周围世界的方式。

sentences.en: The way I think about them is they're sort of two ends of a continuum.
sentences.zh: 我认为它们就像是一个连续体的两端。

sentences.en: You know, a good story is one that's full of detail and creates visual images and emotions.
sentences.zh: 你知道，一个好的故事是充满细节的，能创造出视觉形象和情感。

sentences.en: A good explanation tends to be a bit more abstract.
sentences.zh: 一个好的解释往往更抽象一些。

sentences.en: It might appeal to general features of the world for thinking about science.
sentences.zh: 它可能会诉诸于世界的一般特征来思考科学问题。

sentences.en: It might appeal to scientific laws or regularities.
sentences.zh: 它可能会诉诸于科学定律或规律。

sentences.en: And I think if you look at everyday cases of explanation, we do a mix of storytelling and
sentences.zh: 我认为如果你观察日常生活中解释的案例，我们会将讲故事和

sentences.en: appealing to these more general features of the world.
sentences.zh: 诉诸于这些更普遍的世界特征结合起来。

sentences.en: So for example, if you see a friend arrive late to work and you say, why were you late
sentences.zh: 举个例子，如果你看到朋友上班迟到了，你问她，你为什么上班

sentences.en: to work?
sentences.zh: 迟到了？

sentences.en: The friend might appeal to some general ideas, like there was traffic.
sentences.zh: 朋友可能会诉诸一些普遍的想法，比如交通堵塞。

sentences.en: But she might also tell you how she woke up five minutes later than she intended to, and
sentences.zh: 但她也可能会告诉你，她比原定时间晚起了五分钟，

sentences.en: then she was rushed, and then she burned her toaSt.
sentences.zh: 然后她很匆忙，还烤焦了吐司。

sentences.en: All of these very concrete details that really help you understand from her perspective what
sentences.zh: 所有这些非常具体的细节，真的能让你从她的角度理解

sentences.en: her morning was like and why she's in the emotional state that she's in, and so on.
sentences.zh: 她的早晨是怎样的，以及她为什么处于那种情绪状态，等等。

sentences.en: So I think often we do both of these.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为我们经常两者兼顾。

sentences.en: We do the storytelling, which is very concrete and particular, and we do the explaining, which
sentences.zh: 我们既讲故事，这是非常具体和特殊的，我们也进行解释，这

sentences.en: is much more about extracting the structure of the world in a way that's generalizable.
sentences.zh: 更多是关于以一种可概括的方式提取世界的结构。

sentences.en: And when you say extracting the structure of the world in a way that's generalizable,
sentences.zh: 当你提到“以一种可概括的方式提取世界的结构”时，

sentences.en: what I'm getting from you is that explanations, and to some extent stories as well, are about
sentences.zh: 我从你那里得到的信息是，解释，以及在某种程度上故事，都是关于

sentences.en: constructing models for the world.
sentences.zh: 构建世界模型。

sentences.en: They allow us to cut through confusion, to distill complexity into simplicity.
sentences.zh: 它们让我们能够穿透困惑，将复杂性提炼为简单性。

sentences.en: Yes, I think part of what explanations do is that they relate our observations, which are
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为解释的部分作用在于，它们将我们高度多变、时刻变化的观察结果，

sentences.en: highly variable, changing from moment to moment, to something more like a simple underlying
sentences.zh: 与某种更像是一个简单的底层结构联系起来，

sentences.en: structure that allows us to predict how things might go in the future.
sentences.zh: 这使我们能够预测未来可能会发生什么。

sentences.en: It's a way to try to extract order and regularity from what might otherwise seem disorganized and
sentences.zh: 这是一种试图从看似杂乱无章和令人不安的事物中提取秩序和规律的方法。

sentences.en: unsettling.
sentences.zh: 令人不安。

sentences.en: The more Tanya thought about it, the more she realized that our capacity for explanations
sentences.zh: 坦尼娅思考得越多，就越意识到我们对解释的能力

sentences.en: needed to be studied carefully.
sentences.zh: 需要被仔细研究。

sentences.en: Our drive for explanation itself needed explanation.
sentences.zh: 我们对解释的驱动力本身就需要解释。

sentences.en: For instance, there are times when this drive can make us curious, help us discover new things.
sentences.zh: 例如，有时这种驱动力会让我们好奇，帮助我们发现新事物。

sentences.en: But there are other times when our hunger for a simple story can make us leap to conclusions
sentences.zh: 但有时，我们对简单故事的渴望也会让我们仓促下结论，

sentences.en: and become less curious.
sentences.zh: 从而变得不再那么好奇。

sentences.en: So an everyday example of this that might be familiar to people is the experience of interviewing
sentences.zh: 一个人们可能熟悉的日常例子是面试

sentences.en: someone for a position.
sentences.zh: 某人职位的经历。

sentences.en: When we interview people, often, I think even without realizing it, we construct a whole story
sentences.zh: 当我们面试别人时，我认为即使没有意识到，我们也构建了一个完整的故事，

sentences.en: about the kind of person this is and how they're going to do in the job and how they
sentences.zh: 关于这个人是什么样的人，他们在工作中表现如何，以及他们

sentences.en: fit into what we're looking for.
sentences.zh: 如何符合我们寻找的标准。

sentences.en: And that's one kind of evidence that we might use for deciding who to hire.
sentences.zh: 这是我们决定录用谁时可能使用的一种证据。

sentences.en: But then we also have things like their resume and their letters of reference.
sentences.zh: 但我们也有诸如简历和推荐信之类的东西。

sentences.en: And perhaps we tend to over-rely on our own story that we construct and under-rely on these
sentences.zh: 也许我们倾向于过度依赖自己构建的故事，而低估了这些

sentences.en: other sources of evidence that may or may not fit into our story so nicely.
sentences.zh: 其他可能与我们的故事不那么吻合的证据来源。

sentences.en: So this is not just saying that explanations are sort of deductions we draw from the world.
sentences.zh: 所以这不仅仅是说解释是我们从世界上得出的推论。

sentences.en: It's really saying that explanations are the way we actually see the world.
sentences.zh: 这实际上是说，解释是我们看待世界的方式。

sentences.en: We actually see the world through the explanations and models we build of the world.
sentences.zh: 我们实际上是通过我们构建的世界解释和模型来看待世界的。

sentences.en: One way to think about it is that explanations are the currency in which we understand things.
sentences.zh: 一种思考方式是，解释是我们理解事物的货币。

sentences.en: We're presented with all sorts of information, but we need to do something with it.
sentences.zh: 我们被呈现各种各样的信息，但我们需要用它做点什么。

sentences.en: And the way we do something with it is to construct some sort of a model, an explanatory
sentences.zh: 而我们处理它的方式就是构建某种模型，一种解释性模型，

sentences.en: model, one that we find explanatorily satisfying.
sentences.zh: 一种我们认为在解释上令人满意的模型。

sentences.en: And that's what we use as a basis for thinking and reasoning.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们进行思考和推理的基础。

sentences.en: Well, we'll talk soon about the experiments that you've conducted to analyze our capacity
sentences.zh: 好吧，我们很快会谈谈你为分析我们解释能力

sentences.en: for explanation.
sentences.zh: 而进行的实验。

sentences.en: But I want to start with a story that illustrates so much about our drive for explanation.
sentences.zh: 但我还是想从一个故事开始，它说明了我们对解释的驱动力。

sentences.en: You once drew a link between your daughter's personality and what you knew about her before
sentences.zh: 你曾经在你女儿的个性和你对她出生前

sentences.en: she was born.
sentences.zh: 的了解之间画了一个联系。

sentences.en: Can you explain, Tanya?
sentences.zh: 你能解释一下吗，坦尼娅？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: So when I was pregnant with my first daughter, I discovered around seven months into the pregnancy
sentences.zh: 当我怀上第一个女儿时，我在怀孕七个月左右时发现

sentences.en: that she was breech.
sentences.zh: 她是臀位。

sentences.en: For those of you who haven't gone through this process and aren't familiar with it, that
sentences.zh: 对于那些没有经历过这个过程且不熟悉它的人来说，这

sentences.en: just basically means her head was up rather than down.
sentences.zh: 基本上意味着她的头是朝上的，而不是朝下的。

sentences.en: And that's not where you want it to be before birth.
sentences.zh: 而那不是你希望她在出生前所处的位置。

sentences.en: And so being a good scientist, I did all sorts of research on how she might be able to turn
sentences.zh: 所以作为一个优秀的科学家，我做了各种研究，关于她如何能够转过来，

sentences.en: around and the probability that she would turn around before birth and so on.
sentences.zh: 以及她在出生前转过来的概率等等。

sentences.en: But in fact, she was very comfortable in just the position she was and did not turn around
sentences.zh: 但事实上，她对自己的位置感到非常舒适，并没有在

sentences.en: prior to birth.
sentences.zh: 出生前转过来。

sentences.en: This daughter is now 10, and we still joke that this illustrates her wonderful persistence
sentences.zh: 这个女儿现在10岁了，我们仍然开玩笑说这体现了她极好的坚持

sentences.en: and stubbornness.
sentences.zh: 和固执。

sentences.en: You know, she's very steadfast in the best way that I think will make her an amazing adult
sentences.zh: 你知道，她非常坚定，我认为这种特质会让她成为一个了不起的成年人，

sentences.en: and sometimes a frustrating child.
sentences.zh: 尽管有时她也是个让人头疼的孩子。

sentences.en: You know, of course, on some level, I don't really think there is a connection between
sentences.zh: 当然，在某种程度上，我并不认为两者之间真的有什么联系，

sentences.en: her having been in a breech position before she was born and her being a persistent, stubborn
sentences.zh: 即她出生前是臀位，以及她后来成为一个执着、固执的

sentences.en: child later.
