sentences.en: But it's so tempting to draw these connections and to see these patterns and to try to make
sentences.zh: 但我们总是忍不住去建立这些联系，去寻找这些模式，并试图去

sentences.en: sense of what we observe now in terms of what we know about the paSt.
sentences.zh: 理解我们现在观察到的现象，并将其与我们已知的过去联系起来。

sentences.en: And what I love about this is it shows how indiscriminate we are in coming up with
sentences.zh: 我喜欢这一点的原因是，它展示了我们在为那些本无法解释的事情

sentences.en: explanations for things that otherwise feel inexplicable.
sentences.zh: 寻找解释时，是多么的不加选择。

sentences.en: I think that's right.
sentences.zh: 我想你是对的。

sentences.en: I think very often the world presents us with ambiguity.
sentences.zh: 我认为世界经常向我们呈现出模糊性。

sentences.en: And what we do is we try to connect the dots in a way that tells a compelling narrative and
sentences.zh: 而我们所做的，就是试图把这些点连起来，编织出一个引人入胜的故事，

sentences.en: that allows us to have a sense that there is order.
sentences.zh: 让我们感觉到世界是有序的。

sentences.en: When we come back, we look at the great benefits and the great dangers that are contained in our
sentences.zh: 稍后回来，我们将探讨人类解释世界的驱动力中，所蕴含的巨大益处与巨大危险。

sentences.en: drive to explain the world.
sentences.zh: 你正在收听的是《隐藏的大脑》（Hidden Brain）。

sentences.en: You're listening to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆（Shankar Vedantam）。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 当你还是个孩子的时候，你可能总是会问一个非常重要的问题。

sentences.en: When you were a kid, you've probably asked a very important question all the time.
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么会有云？

sentences.en: Why are there clouds?
sentences.zh: 为什么水会沸腾？

sentences.en: Why does water boil?
sentences.zh: 为什么我会打喷嚏？

sentences.en: Why do I sneeze?
sentences.zh: 如果你已经成年，你可能依然会问“为什么”，尽管问题的内容可能不同。

sentences.en: If you're a grown-up, you might still ask why, even though the questions might be different.
sentences.zh: 为什么我的同事迟到了？

sentences.en: Why is my colleague late?
sentences.zh: 为什么我的狗看起来很忧伤？

sentences.en: Why does my dog seem sad?
sentences.zh: 为什么我的邻居比我更成功？

sentences.en: Why is my neighbor more successful than I am?
sentences.zh: 在普林斯顿大学，心理学家坦尼娅·隆布罗佐（Tanya Lombroso）研究我们那种强大的驱动力，即去理解

sentences.en: At Princeton University, psychologist Tanya Lombroso studies our powerful drive to understand what
sentences.zh: 正在发生什么，去解释这个世界，以及我们对解释的追求能揭示出我们怎样的特质。

sentences.en: it's happening, to explain the world, and what our search for explanations can reveal about us.
sentences.zh: 坦尼娅，你的父亲是一名受过专业训练的电气工程师，在去日本出差期间，

sentences.en: Tanya, your father was trained as an electrical engineer, and during business trips to Japan,
sentences.zh: 他有时会带回一些神秘的小电子礼物给你玩。

sentences.en: he would sometimes bring back mysterious little electronic gifts for you to play with.
sentences.zh: 告诉我你是怎么处理它们的，以及你如何将那段童年经历与你今天作为科学家的研究联系起来。

sentences.en: Tell me what you did with them and the connection that you have made between that childhood experience and your research today as a scientiSt.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我父亲带回这些神秘礼物时有一个规矩，那就是如果我和我哥哥能弄明白它们是怎么工作的，我们就可以留下它们。

sentences.en: Well, my father had a rule when he came back with these mysterious gifts, which was that if my brother and I could figure out how they worked, we could keep them.
sentences.zh: 这很有挑战性，因为上面全是日文，而且它们通常非常陌生。

sentences.en: And this was a challenge because everything was in Japanese, and often they were very unfamiliar.
sentences.zh: 我记得有一次他带回了一个东西，我们最终发现那是一个闹钟，

sentences.en: I remember one time he brought back something, which we eventually discovered was an alarm clock,
sentences.zh: 但它的一侧排列着一系列数字，另一侧也有数字，并且每个数字都有许多小开关。

sentences.en: but it had a series of numbers arrayed on one side and numbers on the other side and lots of little switches for each of the numbers.
sentences.zh: 所以通过正确的数字组合，你可以设定你想让它在什么时间响铃。

sentences.en: And so with the right combination of numbers, you could sort of specify what time you wanted it to sound.
sentences.zh: 所以我们必须做的是观察这些物品的特征，尝试弄清楚不同的按钮是做什么用的，

sentences.en: And so what we had to do was basically look at the features of these artifacts, try to figure out what different buttons they did,
sentences.zh: 思考为什么有人会以那种特定的方式设计它，对吧？

sentences.en: think about why someone might have designed it in that particular way, right?
sentences.zh: 考虑到它是以这种特定方式设计的，它可能是用来做什么的？

sentences.en: What might it be for, given that it was designed in this particular way?
sentences.zh: 那种逆向工程的过程，即观察某样东西的行为、它的外观、它的运作方式，

sentences.en: And that sort of process of reverse engineering, of looking at something's behavior, what it looks like, how it behaves,
sentences.zh: 然后试图反向推导它的功能必然是什么，

sentences.en: and then trying to think backwards to what its function must be,
sentences.zh: 这样你就能理解它为什么具有那些属性。

sentences.en: such that you can understand why it has those properties.
sentences.zh: 这非常像心理学家所做的工作，观察人类行为，然后试图弄清楚大脑为何以那种方式运作。

sentences.en: That's very much what a psychologist does, looking at human behavior, and then trying to figure out why the mind works the way it does.
sentences.zh: 坦尼娅不仅对别人的大脑这样做。

sentences.en: Tanya doesn't just do this with other people's minds.
sentences.zh: 她也对自己这样做。

sentences.en: She does it with her own.
sentences.zh: 例如，有一次她在半夜醒来，因为她听到了一些神秘的声音。

sentences.en: For example, she once woke up in the middle of the night because she heard some mysterious sounds.
sentences.zh: 当然，她做了我们任何人在那种情况下都会做的事。

sentences.en: Of course, she did what any of us would do in that situation.
sentences.zh: 她寻找了一个解释。

sentences.en: She looked for an explanation.
sentences.zh: 那时我女儿大概三岁左右，我母亲正在探访我们。

sentences.en: So this was when my daughter was probably around three, and my mother was visiting.
sentences.zh: 当我听到噪音时，我走出卧室门，发现我母亲和我女儿坐在黑暗中，

sentences.en: And when I heard noise, I went outside of my bedroom door, and I found my mother and my daughter sitting in the dark,
sentences.zh: 正在进行一场正式的茶会，桌子周围摆满了毛绒玩具，还有假装的蛋糕等等。

sentences.en: having a full-blown tea party with stuffed animals around the table and pretend cake and so on.
sentences.zh: 所以我非常困惑。

sentences.en: So I was very puzzled.
sentences.zh: 我也知道我母亲更喜欢在凌晨三点睡觉。

sentences.en: I also know that my mother would prefer to be sleeping at 3 a.m.
sentences.zh: 那么这是怎么发生的呢？

sentences.en: So how had this happened?
sentences.zh: 这似乎是一件需要解释的事情。

sentences.en: This seemed to be something that called out for explanation.
sentences.zh: 那你发现了什么？

sentences.en: And what did you find out?
sentences.zh: 背后的原因是什么？

sentences.en: What was behind it?
sentences.zh: 我发现我女儿醒了，而且非常兴奋，因为她的祖母在探访她。

sentences.en: What I discovered was that my daughter had woken up and was very enthusiastic that her grandmother was visiting.
sentences.zh: 所以她直接下楼去叫醒了我母亲。

sentences.en: So went straight downstairs to wake up my mother.
sentences.zh: 当我母亲被叫醒时，她并不觉得天黑很奇怪，因为我女儿经常在日出前醒来。

sentences.en: And when my mother was woken up, she didn't think it was strange that it was dark because my daughter often woke up before the sun came up.
sentences.zh: 所以她只是以为是早晨。

sentences.en: So she just thought it was morning.
sentences.zh: 现在，你可能会在这一点上说，这太不像话了。

sentences.en: Now, you could just say at this point, this is unacceptable.
sentences.zh: 现在是凌晨三点。

sentences.en: It's 3 o'clock in the morning.
sentences.zh: 回床上睡觉去。

sentences.en: Go back to bed.
sentences.zh: 让他们俩都回床上睡觉，然后自己也回去睡觉。

sentences.en: Send them both back to bed and go back to sleep.
sentences.zh: 但在某些方面，这对你来说是不够的。

sentences.en: But in some ways, that was inadequate for you.
sentences.zh: 你实际上想知道他们为什么会在那里。

sentences.en: You actually wanted to know why they were there.
sentences.zh: 找出原因对你来说很重要。

sentences.en: It was important to you for you to find out.
sentences.zh: 解释发生了什么，对于知道对你所看到的事情做出正确的反应实际上非常重要。

sentences.en: Explaining what happened is actually really important to knowing what the correct response is to the thing that you're seeing.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 我认为这对于预测它何时会再次发生，对于能够促成它或防止它发生也非常重要，

sentences.en: I think it's also very important to being able to anticipate when it will happen again, to being able to bring it about more or to prevent it,
sentences.zh: 这取决于它是我们想要的结果，还是我们倾向于避免的结果。

sentences.en: depending on whether it's an outcome that we want or prefer to avoid.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为我们从对事件的解释中获益良多，尤其是当它涉及人以及关于责任和指责的担忧时。

sentences.en: So I think that there's a lot we get out of an explanation for an event, especially when it involves people and concerns about responsibility and blame.
sentences.zh: 确切地知道某人为什么那样做是非常重要的。

sentences.en: And knowing exactly why someone acted the way they did is incredibly important.
sentences.zh: 我们之前谈到了解释在创造一个更可预测的世界方面为我们提供的价值。

sentences.en: We talked earlier about the value that explanations provide us in terms of producing a world that is more predictable.
sentences.zh: 你能再多谈谈这个想法吗？

sentences.en: Can you talk about this idea a little more?
sentences.zh: 我想到的是体育世界。

sentences.en: I'm thinking about the world of sports.
sentences.zh: 双方球员在进攻和防守上的良好结合。

sentences.en: A good combination of attacking and defending from both guys.
sentences.zh: 如果你理解对手正在使用的策略，而不仅仅是应对对手当下所做的任何动作，

sentences.en: If you understand the strategy an opponent is using, not just sort of responding to whatever your opponent is doing in the moment,
sentences.zh: 竞争就会变得容易得多，获胜也会容易得多。

sentences.en: it becomes much easier to compete and much easier to win.
sentences.zh: 那是一个很好的例子。

sentences.en: That's a great example.
sentences.zh: 我承认我不了解体育世界。

sentences.en: I will confess I do not understand the world of sports.
sentences.zh: 所以我相信你说的话，但这很有道理。

sentences.en: So I will take your word for it, but that makes sense.
sentences.zh: 但我认为这通常是适用的。

sentences.en: But I think it's generally the case.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果你考虑试图预测某人的行为，对吧，也许你有一个死对头，你正试图预测他们的下一步行动。

sentences.en: I mean, if you think about trying to anticipate somebody's behavior, right, perhaps you have an arch nemesis and you're trying to anticipate their next move.
sentences.zh: 如果你理解是什么在激励他们，他们为什么会那样做？

sentences.en: If you understand what's motivating them, why are they acting the way they are?
sentences.zh: 他们的目标是什么？

sentences.en: What's their goal?
sentences.zh: 如果你有了这些问题的答案，你就能处于更有利的位置来预测他们要做什么，并有可能阻止它。

sentences.en: If you have answers to those questions, you'll be in a much better position to anticipate what they're going to do and potentially to prevent it.
sentences.zh: 当我阅读你的作品时，我意识到，你知道，我们不仅从我们发现的解释中受益。

sentences.en: And as I was reading your work, I was realizing that, you know, we don't just benefit from the explanations that we discover.
sentences.zh: 我们还从我们之前的许多人类的解释中受益。

sentences.en: We benefit from the explanations of many human beings who came before us.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你甚至可以说文化是一种将解释从一代传给下一代的机制。

sentences.en: I mean, you might even argue that culture is a mechanism to transmit explanations from one generation to the next.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 我认为通常当我们考虑从解释中学习时，我们想到的是从我们从其他人或书籍中获得的解释中学习。

sentences.en: I think typically when we think about learning from explanations, what we have in mind is learning from the explanations that we receive from other people or from books.
sentences.zh: 我认为也许不太被认可但同样重要的是，我们也通过自己尝试获得解释来学习。

sentences.en: I think it's perhaps less recognized but equally important that we also learn by trying to get explanations ourselves.
sentences.zh: 有时这会激励我们去获取证据并进行新的观察，但有时我们仅仅通过尝试向自己解释就能学到新东西。

sentences.en: Sometimes that motivates us to get evidence and make new observations, but sometimes we can learn something new just by trying to explain to ourselves.
sentences.zh: 有一种现象叫做“自我解释效应”，我想大多数人可能都经历过。

sentences.en: There's a phenomenon called the self-explanation effect that I think most people have probably experienced.
sentences.zh: 那就是因为试图向自己或他人解释某事，从而更好地理解了某事的经历。

sentences.en: And that's the experience of coming to understand something better as a result of trying to explain it to yourself or to somebody else.
sentences.zh: 这种现象中神秘而令人惊奇的一部分是，这是一种即使你没有从其他人或外部世界获得新信息也能发生的学习。

sentences.en: Part of what's sort of mysterious and amazing about the phenomenon is that that's a kind of learning that occurs even though you're not getting new information from anybody else or from the external world.
sentences.zh: 你只是在重新整理和审视你脑子里已有的东西。

sentences.en: You're just rearranging and scrutinizing what's already in your head.
sentences.zh: 在这样做的过程中，你有时会产生一种“顿悟”时刻，并意识到你更好地理解了某件事。

sentences.en: And in the course of doing that, you can sometimes have one of these aha moments and come to realize that you understand something better.
sentences.zh: 或者有时意识到你以为自己理解了某事，但实际上你的知识中存在一个需要填补的重要空白。

sentences.en: Or sometimes come to realize that you thought you understood something, but that there's actually an important gap in your knowledge that you need to fill.
sentences.zh: 造成这种情况的原因之一是所谓的“解释深度错觉”。

sentences.en: One of the reasons for this is something called the illusion of explanatory depth.
sentences.zh: 你刚才提到了这一点。

sentences.en: And you hinted at this just a second ago.
sentences.zh: 坦尼娅，你能拆解一下这个概念吗？

sentences.en: Can you unpack what that idea is, Tanya?
sentences.zh: 是的，当然。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 我们许多人觉得我们了解日常生活中许多设备是如何工作的。

sentences.en: Many of us feel like we understand how a lot of the devices in our everyday life work.
sentences.zh: 我们了解自行车是如何工作的。

sentences.en: We understand how a bicycle works.
sentences.zh: 我们了解微波炉是如何工作的，拉链是如何工作的，等等。

sentences.en: We understand how a microwave works, how a zipper works, and so on.
sentences.zh: 如果你问人们，他们通常会说，是的，我了解拉链是如何工作的。

sentences.en: If you ask people, they'll typically say, yeah, I understand how a zipper works.
sentences.zh: 然后你说，好吧，你能解释一下吗？

sentences.en: And then you say, okay, can you please explain it?
sentences.zh: 当人们真正尝试解释像拉链如何工作这样的事情时，他们开始意识到，也许他们真的没有完全掌握拉链工作的全部细节。

sentences.en: And what happens when people actually try to explain something like how a zipper works is they start to appreciate all of the ways in which maybe they really don't have the full story of how a zipper works.
sentences.zh: 而试图生成一个好的解释的过程，有助于我们意识到我们确实有所欠缺。

sentences.en: And the process of trying to generate a good explanation helps us appreciate that we're really falling short.
sentences.zh: 我见过一些实验，比如你让人们画一辆自行车，人们会画一条连接自行车两个轮子的链条，当然，

sentences.en: I've seen experiments where you ask people to draw a bicycle, for example, and people will draw a chain that connects the two wheels of the bicycle together, which, of course,
sentences.zh: 这会让自行车根本无法骑行。

sentences.en: would make the bicycle impossible to actually ride.
sentences.zh: 你会很快意识到，即使是极其基础的事情，我们实际上可能并不太了解它们是如何工作的。

sentences.en: And you realize very quickly that even when it comes to extremely basic things, we might actually not understand very well how they work.
sentences.zh: 但这实际上需要我们被当场考问，才能揭示出我们知识中的这个空白。

sentences.en: But it actually requires us to be put on the spot to be able to reveal this gap in our knowledge.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 心理学家有时会谈论所谓的“元认知”，也就是我们关于自身认知的认知。

sentences.en: Psychologists sometimes talk about what's called metacognition, which is sort of our cognition about our own cognition.
sentences.zh: 而这种情况就是我们的元认知往往是错误的。

sentences.en: And this is the case where our metacognition is often wrong.
sentences.zh: 我们经常以为自己知道某些实际上并不知道的事情。

sentences.en: We often think we know something that we actually don't know.
sentences.zh: 而在试图解释它的过程中，我们可以更好地校准自己，并意识到我们知道什么，不知道什么。

sentences.en: And in the process of trying to explain it, we can get better calibrated and appreciate what we do when we don't know.
sentences.zh: 我认为这就是尝试解释之所以能如此强大的原因之一。

sentences.en: I think that's one of the reasons trying to explain can be really powerful.
sentences.zh: 但我认为在其他情况下，它实际上不仅可以帮助你识别空白，甚至可以填补它们。

sentences.en: But I think in other cases, it can also actually help you not just recognize gaps, but even fill them.
sentences.zh: 坦尼娅引用了PBS电视剧《比彻姆大宅》（Beecham House）中的一个场景。

sentences.en: Tanya cites a scene from the PBS TV series Beecham House.
sentences.zh: 故事背景设定在18世纪末的印度。

sentences.en: It's set in India in the late 18th century.
sentences.zh: 一名英国人被指控从皇帝那里偷窃，被关进了牢房。

sentences.en: An Englishman has been accused of having stolen from the emperor, and he's put in a jail cell.
sentences.zh: 所以他待在牢房里，试图向自己解释这是怎么发生的。

sentences.en: And so he's in his jail cell, trying to explain to himself how this happened.
sentences.zh: 他在心里想，你知道，谁会背叛我？

sentences.en: And he's thinking to himself, you know, who could have betrayed me?
sentences.zh: 他们为什么要背叛我？

sentences.en: Why would they have betrayed me?
sentences.zh: 皇帝怎么会知道赃物在我家里的什么地方，等等。

sentences.en: How could the emperor have known where the stolen property was in my house and so on?
sentences.zh: 而在那个牢房里，他没有得到任何新信息。

sentences.en: And from that jail cell, he doesn't get any new information.
sentences.zh: 他没有任何新的证据。

sentences.en: He doesn't have any new piece of evidence.
sentences.zh: 然而，仅仅通过思考，通过思考他已经拥有的所有证据，就让他产生了顿悟时刻，意识到是谁背叛了他。

sentences.en: And yet just thinking it through and thinking about all of the pieces of evidence he already had allows him to have the aha moment where he realizes who has betrayed him.
sentences.zh: 有了这个新的洞察，这位英国人与真正的罪犯对质。

sentences.en: With this new insight, the Englishman confronts the true perpetrator of the crime.
sentences.zh: 你知道有无数的嫌疑人。

sentences.en: You know there are innumerable candidates.
sentences.zh: 我得出了一个简单的问题。

sentences.en: I have arrived at one simple question.
sentences.zh: 谁获益最大？

sentences.en: Who had the most to gain?
sentences.zh: 我现在意识到，你并不是在加尔各答的狗展上偶然遇到我母亲的。

sentences.en: I realize now, you did not meet my mother by chance at the dogs in Calcutta.
sentences.zh: 你是蓄意在那里的。

sentences.en: You were there by design.
sentences.zh: 你确切地知道她要去哪里，以及她什么时候会离开。

sentences.en: You knew exactly where she was going and when she would leave.
sentences.zh: 你可能已经监视她好几个月了。

sentences.en: You'd probably be monitoring her for months.
sentences.zh: 所以，有时我们通过获取新证据或询问他人来学习。

sentences.en: So, sometimes we learn by getting new evidence or by asking other people.
sentences.zh: 但有时我们仅仅通过以正确的方式思考事物就能学习。

sentences.en: But sometimes we learn just by thinking about things in the right way.
sentences.zh: 这是一个我称之为“通过思考来学习”的过程。

sentences.en: It's a process I refer to as learning by thinking.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，是通过尝试向自己解释来学习。

sentences.en: In this case, learning by trying to explain to yourself.
sentences.zh: 你知道，前段时间在《隐藏的大脑》中，我们采访了研究员维拉·托宾（Vera Tobin）。

sentences.en: You know, some time ago on Hidden Brain, we spoke with the researcher Vera Tobin.
sentences.zh: 她研究讲故事的人利用我们认知系统所使用的技巧。

sentences.en: She studies the techniques that storytellers use to take advantage of our cognitive systeMs.
sentences.zh: 她说的话和你刚才告诉我的非常接近。

sentences.en: And she said something that is very close to what you just told me a second ago.
sentences.zh: 她说的话和你刚才告诉我的非常接近。

sentences.en: I want to play you a short clip of what she said.
sentences.zh: 我想给你播放一小段她所说的话。

sentences.en: What a story can do for you is construct this insight experience where you feel not that something has blindsided you or that you were just taken by surprise.
sentences.zh: 故事能为你做的是构建这种洞察体验，让你感觉到的不是某事让你措手不及，也不是你仅仅被突如其来的事情惊到了。

sentences.en: But this experience that feels as if you have a real aha moment about how things fit together.
sentences.zh: 而是这种感觉就像你对事物如何组合在一起有了真正的顿悟时刻的体验。

sentences.en: And that is something that humans like a lot.
sentences.zh: 而这正是人类非常喜欢的东西。

sentences.en: So, the two things that jump out at me when I hear Vera say that, Tanya, is that storytellers are doing two things.
sentences.zh: 所以，当我听到维拉（Vera）说那番话时，塔尼娅（Tanya），有两点让我印象深刻，那就是讲故事的人在做两件事。

sentences.en: One, they're actually constructing a story that has mystery and confusion and uncertainty built into it.
sentences.zh: 第一，他们实际上是在构建一个内置了神秘、困惑和不确定性的故事。

sentences.en: And because we find those things aversive, it actually serves as a hook that keeps us listening, keeps us watching, keeps us reading.
sentences.zh: 正因为我们觉得这些东西令人反感，它实际上起到了一个钩子的作用，让我们一直听下去、看下去、读下去。

sentences.en: And then when the explanation is provided, it provides us with this burst of pleasure because we suddenly understand that the mystery is resolved, the puzzle is solved.
sentences.zh: 然后当解释提供出来时，它带给我们一种快感，因为我们突然明白谜题解开了，难题解决了。

sentences.en: Yes, I love that example.
sentences.zh: 是的，我很喜欢那个例子。

sentences.en: And I would also add that science can often have that character as well.
sentences.zh: 我还要补充一点，科学往往也具有这种特质。

sentences.en: You know, so in the case of a good story, there's an author crafting the story to have just the right form.
sentences.zh: 你知道，对于一个好故事来说，有一个作者在精心构思，让故事呈现出恰到好处的形式。

sentences.en: But I think part of what makes science very satisfying is that some of the time we get that experience as well of having all of these clues and then getting the satisfying theory that makes all of those clues fit together in a way that makes sense.
sentences.zh: 但我认为科学之所以令人非常满足，部分原因在于有时我们也会有这种体验：拥有了所有这些线索，然后得到了一个令人满意的理论，将所有线索以一种合乎逻辑的方式串联起来。

sentences.en: I want to talk a moment about situations where explanations do not feel pleasurable.
sentences.zh: 我想花点时间谈谈那些解释让人感觉不愉快的状况。

sentences.en: We've all had the experience of watching a magic trick and being amazed and then discovering the explanation behind the trick.
sentences.zh: 我们都有过这样的经历：看魔术表演时感到惊奇，然后发现了魔术背后的解释。

sentences.en: And invariably, this does not produce wonder, but it produces disappointment, something that, in fact, appeared wondrous, turns out to be, you know, pedestrian.
sentences.zh: 而无一例外，这并不会产生惊叹，反而产生失望；事实上，看起来奇妙的东西，结果却变得平淡无奇。

sentences.en: What do you think this reveals about the explanatory system in the brain?
sentences.zh: 你认为这揭示了大脑中的解释系统什么问题？

sentences.en: One thing that I think it tells us is that there might be cases where we actually find uncertainty and mystery and awe somewhat pleasurable.
sentences.zh: 我认为它告诉我们的一件事是，在某些情况下，我们实际上会觉得不确定性、神秘感和敬畏感有点令人愉悦。

sentences.en: I think if you think about an emotion like awe, it has possibly a kind of negative tinge, right?
sentences.zh: 我想如果你思考像敬畏这样的情绪，它可能带有一种负面的色彩，对吧？

sentences.en: It can be kind of scary to have uncertainty and not understand something.
sentences.zh: 面对不确定性且无法理解某事可能会让人感到有点害怕。

sentences.en: But there's also a way in which it can be pleasurable.
sentences.zh: 但它也有令人愉悦的一面。

sentences.en: It tells us there's something to learn here.
sentences.zh: 它告诉我们这里有东西值得学习。

sentences.en: Here's something that's worth paying attention to.
sentences.zh: 这里有值得关注的东西。

sentences.en: So when we have something that seems to defy the laws of physics or the laws of probability, and it turns out it was just something completely mundane,
sentences.zh: 所以，当我们遇到似乎违背物理定律或概率定律的事情，结果发现它只是极其平凡的事情时，

sentences.en: I think there's a violation between our sense that there was something really amazing to be learned or discovered,
sentences.zh: 我认为这违背了我们认为有某种真正令人惊奇的东西值得学习或发现的感觉，

sentences.en: and then the reality that actually it was just business as usual.
sentences.zh: 而现实却是，这不过是照常营业。

sentences.en: So one thing that we find is that people are more curious about the answers to questions about science than about religion.
sentences.zh: 所以我们发现的一件事是，人们对科学问题的答案比对宗教问题的答案更好奇。

sentences.en: They think that we should answer science questions more than we should answer questions about religion.
sentences.zh: 他们认为我们应该回答科学问题，而不是回答关于宗教的问题。

sentences.en: If I ask you, why is rust red?
sentences.zh: 如果我问你，为什么铁锈是红色的？

sentences.en: And I say, it's a mystery.
sentences.zh: 我说，这是一个谜。

sentences.en: That just seems wrong.
sentences.zh: 这看起来就不对。

sentences.en: But if I say, why does God exist?
sentences.zh: 但如果我说，为什么上帝存在？

sentences.en: It's a mystery.
sentences.zh: 这是一个谜。

sentences.en: Why did Jesus walk on water?
sentences.zh: 为什么耶稣能在水上行走？

sentences.en: It's a mystery.
sentences.zh: 这是一个谜。

sentences.en: For a lot of questions about religion, it's not just that we don't know.
sentences.zh: 对于许多关于宗教的问题，不仅仅是我们不知道。

sentences.en: It's that we seem to be much more comfortable with the idea that we can't know and perhaps that we shouldn't know.
sentences.zh: 而是我们似乎对“我们无法知道，或许也不应该知道”这个想法感到自在得多。

sentences.en: And what do you think spells the difference?
sentences.zh: 你认为是什么造成了这种差异？

sentences.en: Why is it that for some things we actually think that it's unacceptable that you tell me that there's no answer to this?
sentences.zh: 为什么对于某些事情，我们认为你告诉我“这没有答案”是不可接受的？

sentences.en: And for other things, I feel like it's unacceptable that you tell me that there is an answer to it.
sentences.zh: 而对于其他事情，我觉得你告诉我“这有一个答案”是不可接受的？

sentences.en: I think there's a few factors in play.
sentences.zh: 我认为有几个因素在起作用。

sentences.en: I think one of them is that our beliefs play all sorts of different kinds of roles for us.
sentences.zh: 我认为其中之一是我们的信念为我们扮演了各种各样的角色。

sentences.en: One reason that we have the beliefs that we do and that we aspire to have particular kinds of beliefs is because we want to be accurate and represent the world in a way that will give us a model that allows us to predict what will happen.
sentences.zh: 我们之所以拥有现在的信念，并渴望拥有特定类型的信念，原因之一是我们想要准确，并以一种能为我们提供模型的方式来呈现世界，从而让我们能够预测未来会发生什么。

sentences.en: But our beliefs also play important social roles.
sentences.zh: 但我们的信念也扮演着重要的社会角色。

sentences.en: They play important moral roles.
sentences.zh: 它们扮演着重要的道德角色。

sentences.en: They play important personal roles.
sentences.zh: 它们扮演着重要的个人角色。

sentences.en: And I think sometimes in a case like religion or relationships to particular people or institutions,
sentences.zh: 我认为有时在宗教或与特定个人或机构的关系这类案例中，

sentences.en: demanding an explanation might compete with other kinds of goals related to relationships and truSt.
sentences.zh: 要求解释可能会与关系和信任相关的其他目标发生冲突。

sentences.en: We also have evidence that there are some cases where people are uncomfortable with the idea that science could fully explain the human mind.
sentences.zh: 我们还有证据表明，在某些情况下，人们对科学能够完全解释人类思维的想法感到不舒服。

sentences.en: So, for example, people seem to in general be very comfortable thinking that science could explain why we forget things or how stereo vision works or how motor control works.
sentences.zh: 例如，人们似乎普遍非常乐于认为科学可以解释为什么我们会忘记事情，或者立体视觉是如何工作的，或者运动控制是如何工作的。

sentences.en: But they're much less comfortable with the idea that science could explain our religious beliefs or our moral behavior or spiritual experience or appreciation for art.
sentences.zh: 但他们对科学可以解释我们的宗教信仰、道德行为、精神体验或对艺术的欣赏这一想法感到非常不自在。

sentences.en: So all of these phenomena are phenomena that we have a rich internal experience that we feel like we have special access to as the person who is experiencing them.
sentences.zh: 所以所有这些现象都是我们拥有丰富内在体验的现象，作为体验者，我们觉得我们拥有特殊的访问权限。

sentences.en: And for those phenomena,
sentences.zh: 对于这些现象，

sentences.en: it also seems like people think there might be a sort of threat to the idea that somebody outside of our own mind who isn't having those rich personal experiences could provide a full explanation.
sentences.zh: 人们似乎也认为，对于那些没有这种丰富个人体验的外部人员能够提供完整解释的想法，可能存在某种威胁。

sentences.en: I'm wondering,
sentences.zh: 我在想，

sentences.en: tell me what you think of this hypothesis that part of what we're doing when we're trying to explain things is we're trying to make the outside world comprehensible to the inside world.
sentences.zh: 告诉我你对这个假设有什么看法：我们试图解释事物时，部分原因是我们试图让外部世界对内在世界变得可理解。

sentences.en: But there are things in the inside world that already feel comprehensible to us.
sentences.zh: 但内在世界中有些东西我们已经觉得可以理解了。

sentences.en: And for those things, an explanation from the outside does not feel welcome, but it actually feels like an intrusion.
sentences.zh: 对于这些东西，来自外部的解释感觉并不受欢迎，反而感觉像是一种入侵。

sentences.en: I think that's a really interesting idea.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个非常有趣的想法。

sentences.en: As a psychologist, of course, I want to resist that because my job is precisely explaining the internal world.
sentences.zh: 作为一名心理学家，我当然想抵制这一点，因为我的工作正是解释内在世界。

sentences.en: But I think what you describe is capturing something of many people's experience.
sentences.zh: 但我认为你所描述的捕捉到了许多人的体验。

sentences.en: Sometimes people talk about the idea that we are intuitive dualists like Descartes.
sentences.zh: 有时人们谈论我们是像笛卡尔那样的直觉二元论者的观点。

sentences.en: We think of the mind as somehow fundamentally separate from the body.
sentences.zh: 我们认为心灵在根本上与身体是分离的。

sentences.en: And so part of what's going on in some of these cases, I think, is that by trying to give an external or scientific explanation to our internal experience,
sentences.zh: 所以我认为在其中一些案例中，正在发生的事情的一部分是，通过试图给我们的内在体验提供外部或科学的解释，

sentences.en: we are crossing those levels in an uncomfortable way.
sentences.zh: 我们正在以一种令人不舒服的方式跨越这些层面。

sentences.en: We're trying to explain aspects of the mental by appeal to aspects of the biological or the physical.
sentences.zh: 我们试图通过诉诸生物学或物理学的层面来解释心理层面。

sentences.en: When we come back, how our drive for explanations can sometimes lead to disaster.
sentences.zh: 回来后，我们将探讨我们对解释的驱动力有时如何导致灾难。

sentences.en: You're listening to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 你正在收听的是《隐藏的大脑》（Hidden Brain）。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆（Shankar Vedantam）。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: Human beings seem to possess an innate drive to come up with explanations for things.
sentences.zh: 人类似乎拥有一种为事物寻找解释的内在驱动力。

sentences.en: This drive makes us curious, helps us discover things.
sentences.zh: 这种驱动力使我们好奇，帮助我们发现事物。

sentences.en: But as much as our capacity for explanation is impressive and useful,
sentences.zh: 但尽管我们解释的能力令人印象深刻且有用，

sentences.en: psychologist Tanya Lombroso has also found there are important ways in which this drive can lead us astray.
sentences.zh: 心理学家塔尼娅·隆布罗佐（Tanya Lombroso）也发现，这种驱动力在很多重要方面可能会把我们引入歧途。

sentences.en: Tanya, some years ago, researchers from the University of Wisconsin had kids listen to a children's story.
sentences.zh: 塔尼娅，几年前，威斯康星大学的研究人员让孩子们听了一个儿童故事。

sentences.en: It was from the series Clifford, the Big Red Dog.
sentences.zh: 它来自《大红狗克利福德》（Clifford, the Big Red Dog）系列。

sentences.en: One day, Clifford and his friends discovered a new dog who wants to play with them.
sentences.zh: 有一天，克利福德和他的朋友们发现了一只想要和他们一起玩的新狗。

sentences.en: But this dog is different from them in an important way.
sentences.zh: 但这只狗在重要方面与他们不同。

sentences.en: I want to play you a short clip from the television version of the story.
sentences.zh: 我想给你播放一小段该故事电视版的片段。

sentences.en: What a nice guy.
sentences.zh: 真是个好家伙。

sentences.en: He's only got three legs, Clifford.
sentences.zh: 他只有三条腿，克利福德。

sentences.en: Oh my gosh.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: So, let's play.
sentences.zh: 那么，我们来玩吧。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: So, Tanya, what did the RESET study ask and what did it find?
sentences.zh: 那么，塔尼娅，RESET研究问了什么，又发现了什么？

sentences.en: In this study, people were interested in children's ability to extract the moral or the lesson of the story.
sentences.zh: 在这项研究中，人们对儿童提取故事寓意或教训的能力很感兴趣。

sentences.en: And as you can probably imagine in this case with Clifford and the three-legged dog,
sentences.zh: 正如你可能想象的那样，在这个关于克利福德和三条腿狗的案例中，

sentences.en: part of what the story was going for was a general lesson about accepting others who might be different from ourselves, about inclusion and so on.
sentences.zh: 故事的一部分目的是传达一个关于接纳可能与我们不同的人、关于包容等等的普遍教训。

sentences.en: But in fact, overwhelmingly, when children were asked about the lesson, they drew a blank or they drew a much, much more specific lesson or moral, like,
sentences.zh: 但事实上，绝大多数情况下，当孩子们被问及教训时，他们要么大脑一片空白，要么得出了一个非常、非常具体的教训或道德，比如，

sentences.en: you should be nice to three-legged dogs.
sentences.zh: 你应该对三条腿的狗好一点。

sentences.en: Which is not a completely unreasonable conclusion to draw.
sentences.zh: 这并不是一个完全不合理的结论。

sentences.en: Absolutely not.
sentences.zh: 绝对不是。

sentences.en: I think it makes enormous sense.
sentences.zh: 我认为这非常有道理。

sentences.en: But of course, if that's the lesson you draw from it, you might wonder about the value of reading Aesop's fables and other lessons to our children, right?
sentences.zh: 但当然，如果这就是你从中得出的教训，你可能会怀疑给我们的孩子读《伊索寓言》和其他教训的价值，对吧？

sentences.en: If all they're learning about is how you should act towards tortoises and hares, a lot of what we want is for them to extract some more general lesson.
sentences.zh: 如果他们学到的只是你应该如何对待乌龟和兔子，我们想要的很多是让他们提取出一些更普遍的教训。

sentences.en: To put this another way, you can have different levels of explanations.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，你可以有不同层面的解释。

sentences.en: Sometimes your explanation might be correct in a literal sense, but you miss the larger meaning.
sentences.zh: 有时你的解释在字面上可能是正确的，但你错过了更深层的含义。

sentences.en: Other times, we may focus too much on the big picture.
sentences.zh: 其他时候，我们可能太关注大局了。

sentences.en: Think about what happens when the fire alarm goes off in your office.
sentences.zh: 想想当你的办公室火警响起时会发生什么。

sentences.en: Instead of drawing the simple explanation that something is wrong and you should evacuate the building, you might sit around and wait for a bigger explanation.
sentences.zh: 你可能不会得出“出了问题，你应该撤离大楼”这种简单的解释，而是坐在那里等待一个更大的解释。

sentences.en: Is this a real emergency?
sentences.zh: 这是真正的紧急情况吗？

sentences.en: A drill?
sentences.zh: 还是演习？

sentences.en: I think we often face a trade-off between gathering all of the information and learning as much as possible versus acting in a way that's efficient.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们经常面临在收集所有信息和尽可能多地学习与以高效方式行动之间的权衡。

sentences.en: And we have to decide when we're going to decide that we have enough information and just act.
sentences.zh: 我们必须决定什么时候认定我们已经有了足够的信息并直接行动。

sentences.en: In the case that you just described, there are a couple of different types of errors that you could make, and those errors have very different kinds of costs, right?
sentences.zh: 在你刚才描述的情况下，你可能会犯几种不同类型的错误，而这些错误的代价非常不同，对吧？

sentences.en: So one kind of error that you could make is failing to learn something that might have been valuable,
sentences.zh: 所以你可能犯的一种错误是未能学到一些可能有价值的东西，

sentences.en: like whether or not the fire alarm was caused by microwave popcorn being left too long or by something else.
sentences.zh: 比如火警是否是因为微波炉爆米花放太久引起的，还是其他原因。

sentences.en: But another kind of error that you might make is spending too much time trying to figure out what happened and not leaving the building, and that is a very costly error.
sentences.zh: 但你可能犯的另一种错误是花费太多时间试图弄清楚发生了什么，而没有离开大楼，那是一个代价非常高昂的错误。

sentences.en: So in that kind of case, it seems like you'd probably be making a mistake to err on the side of trying to learn extra rather than act safely or cautiously.
sentences.zh: 所以在那种情况下，如果你为了试图多学一点而冒险，而不是安全或谨慎地行动，那可能是一个错误。

sentences.en: But there's going to be other cases where the cost of failing to learn is the cost that you might want to try to avoid.
sentences.zh: 但也会有其他情况，未能学习的代价是你可能想要避免的代价。

sentences.en: You've also found in other studies that people dislike explanations that are generally very good but that have certain exceptions to the rule.
sentences.zh: 你在其他研究中也发现，人们不喜欢那些通常很好但有某些例外情况的解释。

sentences.en: It seems like one thing that we like in an explanation is that it be broad and exceptionless.
sentences.zh: 似乎我们喜欢的一种解释是它应该是广泛且没有例外的。

sentences.en: And so one thing that might happen is that if you have an explanation that only accounts for why your friend acts the way they do on Monday and Tuesday and Thursday but not on Wednesday,
sentences.zh: 所以可能发生的一件事是，如果你有一个解释只能说明为什么你的朋友在周一、周二和周四那样做，但在周三却不是，

sentences.en: you're going to think I'm missing something, right?
sentences.zh: 你会认为我漏掉了什么，对吧？

sentences.en: That can't be the whole story.
sentences.zh: 那不可能是全部真相。

sentences.en: There's something unsatisfying about that, and you're going to keep looking until you find something that accounts for more of your evidence.
sentences.zh: 这让人感到不满足，你会继续寻找，直到找到能解释更多证据的东西。

sentences.en: But I'm also thinking about how this could actually affect us adversely, which is that the real world, in fact, is a messy place,
sentences.zh: 但我也在思考这实际上会如何对我们产生不利影响，那就是现实世界实际上是一个混乱的地方，

sentences.en: and there are times when a very good rule might actually explain 80% of a phenomenon.
sentences.zh: 有时一个非常好的规则实际上可能解释了80%的现象。

sentences.en: That could be an excellent rule, but the fact that it has 20% of exceptions to that rule, if we start to rule those out as good explanations,
sentences.zh: 那可能是一个极好的规则，但如果它有20%的例外，如果我们开始排除这些作为好的解释，

sentences.en: we might rule out things that could actually be very useful.
sentences.zh: 我们可能会排除那些实际上非常有用的东西。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So one danger of trying to look for a good explanation is that the world is not always well-behaved, as you point out.
sentences.zh: 所以试图寻找一个好解释的一个危险是，正如你指出的那样，世界并不总是循规蹈矩的。

sentences.en: Sometimes the world doesn't provide good explanations.
sentences.zh: 有时世界并不提供好的解释。

sentences.en: Sometimes things just are coincidences or are chance or don't have elegant explanations.
sentences.zh: 有时事情仅仅是巧合，或者是偶然，或者没有优雅的解释。

sentences.en: So we've found in our research that sometimes that can be a good thing because people persist in trying to find a good explanation, and in the course of doing that,
sentences.zh: 所以我们在研究中发现，有时这可能是一件好事，因为人们坚持试图找到一个好的解释，而在这样做的过程中，

sentences.en: they might discover important things about the world.
sentences.zh: 他们可能会发现关于世界的重要事情。

sentences.en: But other times, it might lead them to perseverate and trying to find a good explanation when there's just none to be had.
sentences.zh: 但其他时候，这可能会导致他们在根本没有解释的情况下固执地试图找到一个好的解释。

sentences.en: And if you buy the idea that explanations in some ways provide us with pleasure, there is also potentially a risk here because it could be that some explanations, in fact,
sentences.zh: 如果你认同解释在某些方面带给我们快乐的观点，这里也存在潜在的风险，因为有些解释事实上，

sentences.en: are more pleasurable than others.
sentences.zh: 可能比其他解释更令人愉悦。

sentences.en: In fact, they feel like they fit better.
sentences.zh: 事实上，它们感觉更契合。

sentences.en: They're more enjoyable to contemplate.
sentences.zh: 它们更令人赏心悦目。

sentences.en: And if we're drawn to explanations in part because we derive pleasure from them,
sentences.zh: 如果我们被解释所吸引，部分原因是我们从中获得了快乐，

sentences.en: it's quite likely that from time to time we're going to draw the conclusion that the pleasurable explanation is the right explanation when, in fact, it's not.
sentences.zh: 很有可能我们时不时会得出结论，认为令人愉悦的解释就是正确的解释，而事实上并非如此。

sentences.en: I think that's right.
sentences.zh: 我认为那是对的。

sentences.en: So in my own work, I sometimes talk about explanatory virtues,
sentences.zh: 所以在我的工作中，我有时谈论解释的美德，

sentences.en: which are properties like simplicity that make an explanation good and that are often things that we should be seeking in science and in everyday life.
sentences.zh: 它们是像简单性这样使解释变得好的属性，也是我们在科学和日常生活中经常应该追求的东西。

sentences.en: But we also fall prey to explanatory vices, characteristics of explanations that are seductive and that draw us in,
sentences.zh: 但我们也容易陷入解释的恶习，即那些具有诱惑力并吸引我们的解释特征，

sentences.en: but maybe aren't really good guides to how we ought to think about the world.
sentences.zh: 但可能并不是我们应该如何思考世界的真正好的指南。

sentences.en: How does this body of work play out when it comes to things like polarization and partisanship?
sentences.zh: 当涉及到两极分化和党派之争之类的事情时，这项工作是如何体现的？

sentences.en: Well, I think explanation is sort of a funny process in that it can lead to two very diametrically opposed consequences.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为解释是一个很有趣的过程，因为它可能导致两个截然相反的后果。

sentences.en: So typically when we try to explain something, we're trying to accommodate it in the context of what we already believe.
sentences.zh: 所以通常当我们试图解释某事时，我们是在试图将其纳入我们已经相信的背景中。

sentences.en: Part of what's going to make it simple and compelling is that it fits in with the assumptions that we're already working with.
sentences.zh: 使其简单且令人信服的部分原因在于它符合我们已经使用的假设。

sentences.en: But sometimes trying to explain something might lead us to realize an inadequacy in our current theorizing.
sentences.zh: 但有时试图解释某事可能会导致我们意识到当前理论的不足。

sentences.en: And so it might be the impetus for us to revise our beliefs.
sentences.zh: 因此，这可能是我们修正信念的动力。

sentences.en: And you sometimes see this in the history of science.
sentences.zh: 你有时会在科学史上看到这一点。

sentences.en: So explanation on the one hand can be a way to assimilate everything in the context of what you already believe.
sentences.zh: 所以一方面，解释可以是一种在已有信念背景下同化一切的方式。

sentences.en: And it can also sometimes be a mechanism to spark belief revision and change.
sentences.zh: 它有时也可以成为激发信念修正和改变的机制。

sentences.en: And I think what we see in the case of politics is that overwhelmingly it ends up being a force that allows us to assimilate things in the context of what we already believe.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们在政治案例中看到的是，它最终绝大多数情况下成为了一种让我们在已有信念背景下同化事物力量。

sentences.en: Because often political beliefs are deeply ingrained, tied to people's identities, and so on.
sentences.zh: 因为政治信仰通常根深蒂固，与人们的身份等等联系在一起。

sentences.en: I do think that explanation does have the potential to lead us to change our beliefs and not just to confirm the beliefs that we already have.
sentences.zh: 我确实认为解释确实有潜力引导我们改变信念，而不仅仅是确认我们已经拥有的信念。

sentences.en: But I think the political discourse we see right now makes it difficult for those kinds of conditions to obtain.
sentences.zh: 但我认为我们目前所见的政治话语使得这些条件难以实现。

sentences.en: And it's also the case that when we have strong views about something and we see a disconfirming piece of evidence that comes in,
sentences.zh: 而且事实也确实如此，当我们对某事持有坚定观点，并看到有反面证据出现时，

sentences.en: in some ways it's easier to sort of find a way to discount the disconfirming piece of evidence than to revise the model that we have built up,
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，找到一种方法来否定这些反面证据，要比修正我们已经建立的模型更容易，

sentences.en: especially if that model has been built up over time and with effort, right?
sentences.zh: 尤其是如果那个模型是经过长时间努力建立起来的，对吧？

sentences.en: This is why it's so hard, not just in politics, but in science as well, to let go of pet theories.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么不仅在政治领域，在科学领域，人们也很难放弃自己钟爱的理论。

sentences.en: And you've spent 20 years developing a theory.
sentences.zh: 你花了20年时间去发展一个理论。

sentences.en: It's incredibly painful to let that theory go because some new fact has just arisen.
sentences.zh: 仅仅因为出现了一个新事实就放弃那个理论，这会让人感到极其痛苦。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: Often this is referred to as explaining away, right?
sentences.zh: 这通常被称为“找借口”或“强行解释”，对吧？

sentences.en: So you see a discrepant observation and it's easy to think,
sentences.zh: 所以当你看到一个不一致的观察结果时，很容易会想，

sentences.en: oh, well, there must have been a mistake with a microscope that day.
sentences.zh: 噢，那天显微镜肯定出故障了。

sentences.en: Or somebody must have made a mistake copying down that number.
sentences.zh: 或者有人在抄写那个数字时肯定弄错了。

sentences.en: So we find an alternative explanation that doesn't threaten our core beliefs in that case.
sentences.zh: 因此，在这种情况下，我们会找到一个不会威胁到我们核心信念的替代解释。

sentences.en: And I can see this happening all the time in politics.
sentences.zh: 我能看到这种情况在政治中时时刻刻都在发生。

sentences.en: You have a president whom you don't like and, you know, there's nothing that the president can do that can possibly make you think that this was a good decision
sentences.zh: 你有一位不喜欢的总统，你知道，无论总统做什么，你都不可能认为这是一个好的决定，

sentences.en: because you're filtering everything now through the model that basically says this president is an abomination.
sentences.zh: 因为你现在正通过一个基本认为“这位总统是个祸害”的模型来过滤一切信息。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And you also see it in the way that we think about social groups and stereotypes.
sentences.zh: 你在我们思考社会群体和刻板印象的方式中也能看到这一点。

sentences.en: So if you come across an individual who violates your views about a particular stereotype,
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你遇到一个违反了你对特定刻板印象看法的人，

sentences.en: you could revise the stereotype.
sentences.zh: 你本可以修正那个刻板印象。

sentences.en: But often that's not what people do.
sentences.zh: 但人们往往不会这样做。

sentences.en: Often what people do is say, oh, well, this person doesn't fit the stereotype for such and such reason.
sentences.zh: 人们通常会说，噢，好吧，这个人因为这样那样的原因不符合那个刻板印象。

sentences.en: They come up with an explanation for why that person is an exception.
sentences.zh: 他们会为为什么那个人是个例外找出一个解释。

sentences.en: And doing that then allows them to maintain the belief they had about the general group and to preserve the stereotype.
sentences.zh: 这样做让他们能够维持对该群体的原有信念，并保留那个刻板印象。

sentences.en: You've also cited research about how our drive for explanation and storytelling works in the criminal justice system.
sentences.zh: 你还引用过关于我们的解释驱动力和讲故事的本能如何在刑事司法系统中发挥作用的研究。

sentences.en: Can you talk about that research, about how storytelling and explanations shape the practice of justice?
sentences.zh: 你能谈谈那项研究吗？关于讲故事和解释是如何塑造司法实践的？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: There was a really influential model of juror decision making called the story model that was introduced by Pennington and Hastie.
sentences.zh: 有一个由彭宁顿（Pennington）和黑斯蒂（Hastie）提出的非常有影响力的陪审员决策模型，被称为“故事模型”。

sentences.en: And their idea was that if you think about what a juror is doing as they have evidence presented to them, as they hear testimony,
sentences.zh: 他们的观点是，如果你思考一下陪审员在证据呈现给他们、听取证词时在做什么，

sentences.en: as they hear the prosecution and the defense and so on, is trying to construct something like a mental model that's a story of what happened.
sentences.zh: 当他们听取控辩双方的陈述时，他们是在尝试构建某种心理模型，也就是一个关于所发生之事的“故事”。

sentences.en: And the way people decide whether they're going to convict or not is by evaluating which story is better, which does a better job of accounting for all of the evidence.
sentences.zh: 人们决定是否定罪的方式，就是评估哪个故事更好，哪个故事能更好地解释所有证据。

sentences.en: That might sound sort of innocuous, but it leads to some problematic consequences.
sentences.zh: 这听起来可能没什么害处，但它会导致一些棘手的后果。

sentences.en: So one of them is that if you change the order in which people hear testimony, such that it makes it easier or harder to construct the story that's consistent with the prosecution,
sentences.zh: 其中之一就是，如果你改变人们听取证词的顺序，使其变得更容易或更难构建出与控方一致的故事，

sentences.en: for example, that will affect how likely it is that participants think that that story is the right one.
sentences.zh: 例如，这会影响参与者认为该故事是正确故事的可能性。

sentences.en: In other words, both the defense and the prosecution, you know, hypothetically are presenting the same facts,
sentences.zh: 换句话说，假设控辩双方都在陈述相同的事实，

sentences.en: but one of them is constructing the story of the facts better than the other one.
sentences.zh: 但其中一方比另一方更好地构建了事实的故事。

sentences.en: We're more likely to believe the side that presents the better story.
sentences.zh: 我们更容易相信那个呈现出更好故事的一方。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And in this case,
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，

sentences.en: what makes it a better story is just the fact that it was presented in the right temporal order in which the events unfolded so that it was easier to construct that story in your mind.
sentences.zh: 让它成为一个更好故事的原因，仅仅是因为它是按照事件发生的正确时间顺序呈现的，这样更容易在脑海中构建出那个故事。

sentences.en: On September 11, 2016, this was 15 years after the World Trade Center attack, someone took a photo of the 9-11 memorial, a tribute in light.
sentences.zh: 2016年9月11日，那是世贸中心袭击事件发生15年后，有人拍了一张“9·11”纪念活动“光之致敬”的照片。

sentences.en: Two very powerful blue lights representing the Twin Towers were beamed into the sky.
sentences.zh: 两道代表双子塔的强力蓝光射向天空。

sentences.en: And at the top, there appeared to be a strange, glowing figure.
sentences.zh: 而在顶端，似乎出现了一个奇怪的发光人形。

sentences.en: I want to play you a short news clip.
sentences.zh: 我想给你播放一段简短的新闻片段。

sentences.en: Two powerful lights soar into the air as a tribute to lives lost on 9-11.
sentences.zh: 两道强光冲向天空，以纪念在“9·11”中逝去的生命。

sentences.en: But look closer.
sentences.zh: 但仔细看。

sentences.en: There's an image atop the lights.
sentences.zh: 光束顶端有一个影像。

sentences.en: The photo is now a worldwide sensation.
sentences.zh: 这张照片现在轰动了全球。

sentences.en: Is this a trick of the light?
sentences.zh: 这是光的戏法吗？

sentences.en: Jesus?
sentences.zh: 耶稣？

sentences.en: An angel?
sentences.zh: 天使？

sentences.en: A cross?
sentences.zh: 十字架？

sentences.en: Beautiful.
sentences.zh: 太美了。

sentences.en: Amazing.
sentences.zh: 太神奇了。

sentences.en: Can you talk a moment, Tanya, about the role that some explanations might play in providing us with, in some ways, an emotional defense system,
sentences.zh: 塔尼娅（Tanya），你能谈谈某些解释在为我们提供某种情感防御系统方面所起的作用吗？

sentences.en: a way of sort of reconciling ourselves to things that might otherwise be very painful to contemplate?
sentences.zh: 一种让我们与那些原本可能非常痛苦而难以面对的事情达成和解的方式？

sentences.en: There's some evidence that when people feel uncertainty or a lack of control in their own lives,
sentences.zh: 有一些证据表明，当人们在生活中感到不确定或缺乏控制感时，

sentences.en: one response that they might have is to try to latch on to their ideology or an explanatory framework that gives them a sense of order in the world.
sentences.zh: 他们可能产生的一种反应是试图抓住他们的意识形态或某种解释框架，这能给他们一种世界是有序的感觉。

sentences.en: And for some people, that might be religion.
sentences.zh: 对有些人来说，这可能是宗教。

sentences.en: For other people, it might be a sense that the government is a very stable, powerful force that can provide order.
sentences.zh: 对另一些人来说，这可能是一种认为政府是一个非常稳定、强大的力量，能够提供秩序的感觉。

sentences.en: It could be the idea that science gives us a very orderly picture of the world.
sentences.zh: 也可能是认为科学为我们提供了一个非常有秩序的世界图景。

sentences.en: But it does seem like the idea that there is structure and order and regularity is something that we're drawn to in the face of moments that seem anxiety-provoking and to suggest that maybe the world is just random in a very uncomfortable way.
sentences.zh: 但在面对那些令人焦虑、暗示世界可能以一种非常令人不安的方式随机运行的时刻时，我们似乎确实会被那种认为世界存在结构、秩序和规律的想法所吸引。

sentences.en: I'm thinking about the study that Jennifer Whitson and Adam Gilinski did several years ago.
sentences.zh: 我想到詹妮弗·惠特森（Jennifer Whitson）和亚当·吉林斯基（Adam Gilinski）几年前做的一项研究。

sentences.en: They induced a feeling of a lack of control among volunteers.
sentences.zh: 他们诱导志愿者产生了一种缺乏控制感的感觉。

sentences.en: And they found that compared to a control group, volunteers who experienced a lack of control showed increased pattern recognition in noise.
sentences.zh: 他们发现，与对照组相比，经历过缺乏控制感的志愿者在噪声中表现出了更强的模式识别能力。

sentences.en: So, in other words, when they were shown, like, you know, the static on a television screen, for example, they thought that they could see images in the television screen.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，当给他们看电视屏幕上的雪花点时，他们认为自己能在屏幕上看到图像。

sentences.en: Or when they were shown sort of random, you know, gyrations in the stock market, they felt like they could detect patterns in what was going on.
sentences.zh: 或者当给他们看股市中随机的波动时，他们觉得能从中检测出规律。

sentences.en: And Jennifer Whitson and Adam Gilinski thought that there was some connection between these two things, that in the presence of a feeling of a lack of control,
sentences.zh: 詹妮弗·惠特森和亚当·吉林斯基认为这两者之间存在某种联系，即在感到缺乏控制的情况下，

sentences.en: we actually seek to impose control by seeing patterns where none exiSt.
sentences.zh: 我们实际上是通过在不存在模式的地方看到模式来寻求施加控制。

sentences.en: Can you talk about how this phenomenon connected to your work is potentially behind some of the conspiracy theories we see circulating in the world today?
sentences.zh: 你能谈谈这种与你的工作相关的现象，是如何成为当今世界流传的某些阴谋论背后的潜在原因的吗？

sentences.en: One idea, and I will confess this is somewhat speculative, but you might think of conspiracy theories as an error of over-explaining.
sentences.zh: 有一个观点，我承认这有些推测性，但你可以把阴谋论看作是一种“过度解释”的错误。

sentences.en: Many conspiracy theories have the characteristic that they take lots of observations that might all have independent explanations
sentences.zh: 许多阴谋论的特点是，它们将许多可能都有独立解释的观察结果拿来，

sentences.en: that might sometimes be partially due to chance, and they connect them all to one underlying individual or group that has a particular intention and is carrying out that intention.
sentences.zh: 这些结果有时可能部分归因于偶然，然后将它们全部联系到一个具有特定意图并正在执行该意图的潜在个人或群体身上。

sentences.en: And so, that's a case where maybe there is no satisfying explanation for why these five independent observations came to be and how they unfolded exactly the way they do,
sentences.zh: 所以，这是一种可能对为什么这五个独立的观察结果会发生以及它们究竟是如何展开的没有令人满意的解释的情况，

sentences.en: but the conspiracy theorists impose one.
sentences.zh: 但阴谋论者强加了一个解释。

sentences.en: And certainly, I think you see that these kinds of beliefs can be heightened in the context of uncertainty, lack of power, and so on.
sentences.zh: 当然，我认为你可以看到，在不确定性、缺乏权力等背景下，这类信念会加剧。

sentences.en: And, you know, when you think about the conspiracy theory that the United States government was behind the 9-11 attacks, for example,
sentences.zh: 而且，当你想到美国政府是“9·11”袭击幕后黑手这种阴谋论时，

sentences.en: you know, the complexity of what would be involved in having a conspiracy let that actually work.
sentences.zh: 你知道，要让一个阴谋真正运作起来所涉及的复杂性。

sentences.en: I mean, I live and work in Washington, and I know that you can't tell anything to a group of three people in Washington
sentences.zh: 我是说，我在华盛顿生活和工作，我知道在华盛顿，你不能告诉三个人一组的群体任何事情，

sentences.en: and expect it to be kept a secret for very long.
sentences.zh: 并指望它能保密很长时间。

sentences.en: You know, Washington is full of leaks.
sentences.zh: 你知道，华盛顿到处都是泄密。

sentences.en: And so, the idea that, you know, hundreds or thousands of people across the federal government
sentences.zh: 所以，认为联邦政府中成百上千人

sentences.en: could have kept this massive secret is just completely implausible.
sentences.zh: 能够保守这个巨大的秘密，简直是完全不可信的。

sentences.en: But, of course, that's precisely the conspiracy theory that circulated very widely after the 9-11 attacks
sentences.zh: 但当然，这正是“9·11”袭击后广泛流传的阴谋论，

sentences.en: and was embraced by large numbers of people around the world.
sentences.zh: 并被世界各地大量的人所接受。

sentences.en: I think that's an interesting example because it illustrates a point that we spoke about before,
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个有趣的例子，因为它说明了我们之前谈到的一点，

sentences.en: that there's many different ways in which you might think that an explanation is simple or complex.
sentences.zh: 即对于解释是简单还是复杂，有许多不同的看法。

sentences.en: So, in one way, that conspiracy theory is extremely complicated
sentences.zh: 所以，从某种角度看，那个阴谋论极其复杂，

sentences.en: because all of the details of how the government's plan would have been carried out and carried out effectively
sentences.zh: 因为政府计划如何实施并有效执行的所有细节，

sentences.en: in a way that's consistent with the fact that we didn't have leaks and so on,
sentences.zh: 以及与我们没有泄密等事实相一致的方式，

sentences.en: that's all extremely complicated.
sentences.zh: 这一切都极其复杂。

sentences.en: But the part that's very simple is that many outcomes are all attributed to one underlying entity,
sentences.zh: 但非常简单的那部分是，许多结果都被归因于一个潜在的实体，

sentences.en: in this case, or an organization rather than a single person, with a particular intention.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，或者说是一个组织，而不是某个人，且具有特定的意图。

sentences.en: And so, in that sense, it might be a relatively simple explanation in that it reduces many observations
sentences.zh: 所以，从这个意义上说，它可能是一个相对简单的解释，因为它将许多观察结果简化为

sentences.en: to something that's sort of a simple root cause,
sentences.zh: 某种简单的根本原因，

sentences.en: even though the details of how that root cause manifests in what we observed is extremely complicated.
sentences.zh: 尽管那个根本原因如何在我们观察到的事物中表现出来的细节极其复杂。

sentences.en: We talked earlier in our conversation about the power of explaining in helping us understand things,
sentences.zh: 我们在谈话中早些时候讨论过解释的力量如何帮助我们理解事物，

sentences.en: that it actually could be a mechanism for learning.
sentences.zh: 它实际上可能是一种学习机制。

sentences.en: And you've talked before about how we can utilize this in some ways to combat some of our biases.
sentences.zh: 你之前也谈到过我们如何利用这一点在某种程度上对抗我们的偏见。

sentences.en: So, it is the case that we often seek explanations that match our pre-existing views.
sentences.zh: 确实，我们经常寻求符合我们既有观点的解释。

sentences.en: But how can we use explanations to combat this bias, Tanya?
sentences.zh: 但塔尼娅，我们该如何利用解释来对抗这种偏见呢？

sentences.en: I think there's a few ways in which explanation can help us.
sentences.zh: 我认为解释可以在几个方面帮助我们。

sentences.en: One way it can help us relates to a previous example.
sentences.zh: 它能帮助我们的一个方面与之前的例子有关。

sentences.en: We talked about the case where children will draw the lesson from a story
sentences.zh: 我们谈到了孩子们会从故事中得出教训的情况，

sentences.en: that you should be kind to three-legged dogs,
sentences.zh: 即你应该善待三条腿的狗，

sentences.en: rather than realizing that there's something more general to be learned there.
sentences.zh: 而不是意识到那里还有更普遍的东西可以学习。

sentences.en: What we found in a study looking at cases like that is that just prompting someone to explain
sentences.zh: 我们在研究这类案例时发现，仅仅是提示某人去解释

sentences.en: different parts of the story, why the characters acted the way they did,
sentences.zh: 故事的不同部分，为什么角色会那样做，

sentences.en: why something was the right or wrong thing to do,
sentences.zh: 为什么某件事是正确或错误的做法，

sentences.en: that can lead young children to re-represent the story such that they realize it's not just about a three-legged dog,
sentences.zh: 这可以引导年幼的孩子重新表述故事，从而意识到这不仅仅是关于一只三条腿的狗，

sentences.en: but maybe more generally a story about social inclusion.
sentences.zh: 而可能是一个关于社会包容的更普遍的故事。

sentences.en: So, that's an example of explaining, leading us to change the way we're representing something
sentences.zh: 所以，这是一个解释引导我们改变对某事表述方式的例子，

sentences.en: in a way that helps us appreciate something at a broader level of abstraction.
sentences.zh: 这有助于我们在更广泛的抽象层面上理解事物。

sentences.en: And it's interesting, when it comes to something like fighting conspiracy theories,
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，当涉及到对抗阴谋论之类的事情时，

sentences.en: we really don't practice what you just suggested.
sentences.zh: 我们真的没有实践你刚才建议的方法。

sentences.en: You know, we often believe the way to combat a conspiracy theory is to throw evidence against it.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们通常认为对抗阴谋论的方法是向它抛出证据。

sentences.en: But really, the more effective approach might well be to ask the person with a conspiracy theory
sentences.zh: 但实际上，更有效的方法很可能是要求持有阴谋论的人

sentences.en: to actually explain it in depth to us, and to have them in some ways discover the gaps in their own beliefs
sentences.zh: 向我们深入解释它，并让他们在某种程度上发现自己信念中的漏洞，

sentences.en: that are surfaced by this illusion of explanatory depth.
sentences.zh: 这些漏洞会被这种“解释深度的错觉”所揭示。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: In fact, there's some evidence in the political domain that asking people to explain policies,
sentences.zh: 事实上，在政治领域有一些证据表明，要求人们解释政策，

sentences.en: like how a particular tax policy would work, for example,
sentences.zh: 例如某项特定的税收政策将如何运作，

sentences.en: helps them to appreciate that maybe they don't understand it as well as they thought they did.
sentences.zh: 有助于他们意识到自己可能并不像想象中那样了解它。

sentences.en: And that can induce a kind of humility or an appreciation that you might not be in the best position
sentences.zh: 这可以诱发一种谦逊感，或者意识到你可能并不处于最好的位置

sentences.en: to have a very firm perspective on that political issue
sentences.zh: 去对那个政治议题持有非常坚定的观点，

sentences.en: and perhaps be more open-minded and willing to revise your beliefs.
sentences.zh: 并可能变得更加开放，愿意修正自己的信念。

sentences.en: There's been some work that shows that when we come up with explanations for things,
sentences.zh: 有一些研究表明，当我们为事物想出解释时，

sentences.en: we're more likely to actually believe those explanations.
sentences.zh: 我们更有可能真正相信那些解释。

sentences.en: In other words, if I'm in a debating tournament, for example,
sentences.zh: 换句话说，如果我参加辩论赛，

sentences.en: and I'm randomly assigned to make one case,
sentences.zh: 被随机分配去陈述某一个立场，

sentences.en: I'm more likely to believe the case that I'm making.
sentences.zh: 我更有可能相信我正在陈述的那个立场。

sentences.en: So genuinely, the act of coming up with explanations and arguments
sentences.zh: 所以，提出解释和论点的行为确实

sentences.en: prompts me to actually believe what it is that I'm arguing.
sentences.zh: 促使我真正相信我正在争论的内容。

sentences.en: And you and others have talked about the value of essentially,
sentences.zh: 你和其他人谈到过本质上的价值，

sentences.en: if you want to de-bias yourself, one thing to do is to try and make arguments in favor of both sides,
sentences.zh: 如果你想消除自己的偏见，可以尝试为双方都提出论点，

sentences.en: that the effort of coming up with an argument in favor of both sides
sentences.zh: 为双方提出论点的努力

sentences.en: allows you to see the virtue of different positions that you might not otherwise choose to do.
sentences.zh: 让你能够看到你原本可能不会选择的其他立场的优点。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: So the strategy you just described is sometimes referred to as consider the opposite.
sentences.zh: 所以你刚才描述的策略有时被称为“考虑对立面”。

sentences.en: And it sounds very, very simple, but it's also very powerful and very broadly applicable.
sentences.zh: 它听起来非常、非常简单，但它也非常强大且适用范围极广。

sentences.en: And part of the reason it's so powerful is because it's not something that we tend to do spontaneously.
sentences.zh: 它之所以如此强大，部分原因在于我们往往不会自发地去做这件事。

sentences.en: So if you're asked to consider a particular view or coming up with an explanation for a particular observation,
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你被要求考虑一个特定的观点或为某个特定的观察结果提出解释，

sentences.en: you tend not to spontaneously think, but how might I be wrong?
sentences.zh: 你往往不会自发地想：我可能会错吗？

sentences.en: Or what might some alternative perspectives be?
sentences.zh: 或者还有什么其他的替代视角吗？

sentences.en: But doing that can be a very powerful way to avoid some of the kinds of biases that you refer to.
sentences.zh: 但这样做可以成为避免你提到的某些偏见的一种非常有效的方法。

sentences.en: I'm wondering if there have been times in your life where, looking back,
sentences.zh: 我想知道在你的人生中，是否有过回顾过去时，

sentences.en: you realize that you leaped to the wrong conclusion or drew the wrong explanation.
sentences.zh: 意识到自己草率地得出了错误的结论或做出了错误的解释的时候？

sentences.en: Have there been moments like that when you've looked back at and sort of said,
sentences.zh: 当你回顾过去并对自己说，

sentences.en: uh-oh, I fell prey to the same things that I'm studying?
sentences.zh: “噢，我陷入了自己正在研究的同样的问题中”，有过这样的时刻吗？

sentences.en: I can think of one example when I was a college student.
sentences.zh: 我能想到一个我还是大学生时的例子。

sentences.en: So it was my birthday, and my boyfriend had planned what was supposed to be a nice dinner for me.
sentences.zh: 那天是我生日，我男朋友本打算带我去吃顿美餐。

sentences.en: And on the way to our dinner, he said,
sentences.zh: 在去餐厅的路上，他说：

sentences.en: oh, you know what?
sentences.zh: “噢，你知道吗？

sentences.en: I just need to get these books from the library.
sentences.zh: 我得去图书馆取几本书。

sentences.en: Do you mind if we just stop by and pick up these books?
sentences.zh: 你不介意我们顺路去取一下吧？

sentences.en: Here, you take these call numbers so that we're faSt.
sentences.zh: 给你，这些是索书号，这样我们能快点。”

sentences.en: And my immediate temptation was to fit this into a frustrating pattern of having
sentences.zh: 我当时的第一反应是感到沮丧，觉得这又是那种

sentences.en: taken second place to immediate work concerns and so on, right?
sentences.zh: 总是把工作琐事排在第一位的老套路，对吧？

sentences.en: This was supposed to be my birthday.
sentences.zh: 这可是我的生日啊。

sentences.en: We shouldn't be doing this errand.
sentences.zh: 我们不该去办这种杂事。

sentences.en: And I very shortly discovered I had to revise this assessment because it turns out
sentences.zh: 但很快我就发现自己必须修正这种看法，因为原来

sentences.en: that my then-boyfriend, now-husband, had hidden my birthday presents
sentences.zh: 我当时的男朋友、现在的丈夫，把我的生日礼物

sentences.en: throughout the library at Stanford University under different call numbers.
sentences.zh: 藏在了斯坦福大学图书馆的不同书架上，并对应着不同的索书号。

sentences.en: And so as I was walking around the library trying to get these books,
sentences.zh: 所以，当我走在图书馆里试图找那些书的时候，

sentences.en: I was discovering the hidden gifts hidden in the library.
sentences.zh: 我发现了一个又一个藏在图书馆里的礼物。

sentences.en: What a lovely story.
sentences.zh: 真是个动人的故事。

sentences.en: And I feel like this tells us something really important because, of course,
sentences.zh: 我觉得这告诉了我们一件非常重要的事，因为当然，

sentences.en: the story that we're painting about explanations is not just a story about how we think about
sentences.zh: 我们对解释所构建的故事，不仅仅关乎我们如何看待

sentences.en: politics or how we think about science, but it's also about how we think about the people
sentences.zh: 政治或科学，也关乎我们如何看待生命中

sentences.en: in our lives, our colleagues, our partners, our children, our parents.
sentences.zh: 重要的人，比如同事、伴侣、孩子和父母。

sentences.en: And so often, we're drawing these very quick explanations about why they're doing what
sentences.zh: 我们经常会非常草率地给他们的行为

sentences.en: they're doing.
sentences.zh: 下定义。

sentences.en: And very often, these conclusions are actually wrong.
sentences.zh: 而这些结论往往是错误的。

sentences.en: And we really need to slow down and ask ourselves, how do I know what I think I know?
sentences.zh: 我们真的需要慢下来问问自己：我怎么知道我以为我知道的事情是真的？

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是这样。

sentences.en: I think asking ourselves how we know what we think we know and thinking about
sentences.zh: 我认为问问自己如何得知所谓的“真相”，并思考

sentences.en: alternative explanations are both very powerful tools for trying to overcome
sentences.zh: 其他的解释可能性，是克服我们

sentences.en: some of our tendencies to leap to conclusions and go with our familiar explanations.
sentences.zh: 倾向于仓促下结论和固守固有解释的有力工具。

sentences.zh: 坦尼娅·隆布罗佐（Tanya Lombroso）是一位心理学家，也是普林斯顿大学

sentences.zh: 概念与认知实验室的主任。
